title: Paul Mares and playing with different trumpeters
summary: Mares played well; a driving trumpet drives him; he avoids a bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah, this is that English magazine. I was just checking through here to see if there's any other ideas about your life, any questions here. How did you enjoy working with Joe Merez's brother? I started to say Joe Merez. I'll change this. Paul's. Paul Merez.
He played wonderful. He played wonderful.
I got to hear him and meet him of course too. Is there any advice in playing together that is in harmonies or things that you work on, trumpet and trombone?

Paul is like Muggsy. You have what you call a good drive. And if the trumpet is driving, it makes you drive. That's what I feel. Of course I drive too. If I play with Bobby Haggard, Bobby plays a different style together. To me they all got different styles. You hear Winger, you hear Muggsy, you hear Butterfield, you hear Yank Lawson. They all got different styles.
Do you sometimes consciously try to play sort of a bass part since you don't usually use a string bass in your band or tuba?
That's why I don't want to use a bass because it would interfere with me.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
